svg.text: Spin Plate
Roll the skewer between your palms: an empty place setting and your name blur into one picture, your name on the plate.
cut
fold / score
lemon card #feed95, black print
side A: the empty place setting
what you see at rest, facing you
side B: printed upside-down
(flip about the skewer line = upright)
cut + print (two discs, Ø110, 300 gsm; dashed line = skewer axis)
what the eye gets when it spins (computed)
ideal: 50/50 persistence
3D simulation from the seat
(180 phases / turn, disc flips edge-on)
assembly
disc A + disc B back to back,
skewer sandwiched on the diameter
(2 x 0.4 mm card, 3 mm skewer, PVA)
roll me
two lemon V-cradles hold the skewer ends on the table (name printed small on them)
the physics
Skewer 3 mm, palms sliding past each other at 10 cm/s: omega = 0.2 m/s / 3 mm = 67 rad/s = about 10 turns/s.
Each turn shows A then B: 20 swaps/s, above the ~16 Hz fusion limit of a lamp-lit dinner room (eye integrates ~1/20 s).
Persistence = average of the two images, so ink on one side only reads 50 %; ink on both reads 100 %.
Measured in the sim: name strokes at ~17 % luminance contrast (printed black on lemon is ~89 %). It reads, but it is a ghost.
Disc rotates about the line of the text, so text rows stay near the axis and stay sharp; ring and cutlery smear vertically.
Back side is printed upside-down so it flips upright (thaumatrope rule). Name Ø110: cap 7.2 mm, 0.9 deg at 450 mm.
